title: Hearing Punch at a Carnival day gig
summary: He recounts hearing Punch's band on Carnival day and why he did not take out his horn.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: You hear him around there, Eddie? I never, I heard him a carnival day. I didn't know it was him until I left the place. He was playing upstairs over, opposite Dixie's, you know? Yeah. And Al Rose had asked me to bring my horn around her, so I did. I thought I'd run into Al, but I never didn't. I come around there, but I didn't see Al.
Cause Dixie came out on her, on her gallery and played a-
You didn't recognize me, that was it.
No, played a tune with Punch. Yeah. Yeah, I believe he had four pieces up there, didn't he?
Yeah, they had a slow drag on bass, I think, and Manuel Sayo's on guitar band.

Yeah, well I was looking, I wasn't looking for you, I was looking for Al. Yeah. I didn't see him, so I didn't stay there too long. I remember. Well I had my horn the other night, you know what I mean? But after I seen you all had a horn, a horn in the band, I said to him, I said, well, they ain't no use, me letting these boys know I got my horn. Sure the fuck? I know, boy, but I didn't feel that way, you know? Yeah. He didn't know me, been different if I knew the boy. He didn't know me and I think, you know, I'm trying to chisel in on him. You know some people don't. So I never, I tell you I didn't have my horn, but I had brought my horn with him.
He would have enjoyed it cause he had a bad call that night.
Yeah, I had it in the, in the, in the court.
